channel.title: Honolulu Civil Beat - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Honolulu Civil Beat (civilbeat.org)

item.title: What The Immigration Debate Misses About Place And Belonging
item.description: Human beings should be treated humanely. It's a basic moral minimum, not a political vision.

item.title: Governor Asks Lawmakers For $126M In Green Fee Projects
item.description: Some lawmakers are questioning the administration's plan to fund the projects through a combination of the new fee and bonds.

item.title: Will Disaster Insurance Overhaul Increase Protections For Future Survivors?
item.description: Other states impacted by similar disasters are reforming their insurance laws. Legislators here are teeing up bills to follow suit.

item.title: He Mau Pilikia Mea Kaʻahele Ma Dillingham Ma Muli O Ke Kūkulu Alakau
item.description: Ua wāwahi nā limahana kūkulu i nā alanui a me nā alahele, a he ʻaʻe ʻia paha o kekahi mau kānāwai ADA.

item.title: Red Hill Victims Dealt A Blow In Their Fight Against The Navy
item.description: Plaintiffs said they didn't know about fuel samples until it was too late. The judge declined their request to punish the government.

item.title: Hawaiʻi Mayors Scrap Controversial Tax Pitch In Election Year
item.description: The mayors decided against asking the Legislature for a 20-year extension of the general excise tax surcharge for rail and other transportation projects to allow time for more due diligence.

item.title: HPD Officers Fired For Burglary, Assault And Fraud Could Be Rehired
item.description: Discharges are usually challenged and can be bumped down to suspensions, the records show, allowing cops to return to work.

item.title: What Does It Take To Prove You’re Sick Enough To Get Treatment?
item.description: Hawaiʻi must seriously consider a universal health care system that does not hinge on employment or the outcome of an adversarial hearing.

item.title: Hawaiʻi Wrongly Jailed Him For 20 Years. Reparations Came Too Late
item.description: Alvin Jardine fought for nearly a decade to be paid under the state's wrongful conviction compensation law. He died before receiving payment.

item.title: The Friday Crossword: Super Bowl LX
item.description: Get ready for the Big Game with our latest puzzle.
